subject: Operational zones & shadow deploy patterns for private VPC runtime
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, cloud-ops@acme.com
Cc: eng@netsecure.io
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Operational zones & shadow deploy patterns for private VPC runtime

Team —

Following our run-of show with ACME last week I sketched a lightweight pattern for private VPC -> on-prem runtime rollouts that I think will address two recurring risks we keep seeing: 1) cross-tenant KV cache collision during model variant switch, and 2) customer-side routing surprises during canary.

High level proposal (attached diagrams + playbook):
- Operational zones: split tenant traffic into three soft zones inside the customer VPC: ingress-proxy (north-south), runtime-pool (data-plane compute), and control-plane egress zone (for metrics, state sync, model fetch).
- Shadow deploy pattern: mirror 100% of production requests to a shadow runtime in a separate runtime-pool zone with prefix-aware KV cache keys. Shadow traffic is non-returning (no user response) but exercises path and cache behavior before cutover.
- Egress sharding: provide an egress-shard table per-tenant (attached csv) that maps BGP next-hops to tenant shards for predictable egress enforcement and firewall rules.

Notes on safety:
- Shadow is read-only and disables any persistent state writes (no model promotions).
- KV cache uses tenant-prefixed namespace to avoid collisions. During shadow we append a deterministic suffix so shadow keys never overwrite prod.

Asks:
1) Marcus — can you validate the runtime-pool sizing assumptions on slide 2 (opzones-diagram-v1.png)?
2) Irene — quick sanity check on firewall/BGP implications and whether the sharding table is operationally feasible with ACME infra.
3) ACME/cloud-ops — any constraints on traffic mirroring (pcap limits, mirror session rates)?

I've attached the diagram and a draft playbook. Suggest we discuss Thursday 11am PT if that works.

Thanks,
Rachel

--
Rachel Kim
Program Manager, Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, cloud-ops@acme.com
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational zones & shadow deploy patterns for private VPC runtime

Rachel — nice write-up. Quick inline: 

> Operational zones: split tenant traffic into three soft zones inside the customer VPC: ingress-proxy (north-south), runtime-pool (data-plane compute), and control-plane egress zone (for metrics, state sync, model fetch).

For sizing: the runtime-pool in the diagram assumes a 2x buffer for bursty seq-lengths. That seems reasonable but we should call out the CPU/GPU packing targets per node class (e.g., T4/RTX-6000) and the expected token/sec distribution. I flagged a comment on slide 3 with numbers.

> Shadow deploy pattern: mirror 100% of production requests to a shadow runtime in a separate runtime-pool zone with prefix-aware KV cache keys.

Two notes: 
- Mirroring 100% might be overkill for initial verification; can we phase: 10% -> 50% -> 100% to avoid overwhelming shadow resources?
- Shadow prefixing is correct, but we also need a TTL policy so shadow cache entries don't bloat memory. Suggest 10-minute TTL during shadow run.

I'll drop a revised sizing table into the Drive link. Happy to cover the kernel/packing numbers on Thurs.

—Marcus
Senior SRE, Serving Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, eng@netsecure.io, cloud-ops@acme.com
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational zones & shadow deploy patterns for private VPC runtime

Thanks for the draft — a few operational concerns from the network/security side: 

1) Egress sharding + BGP: the attached egress-shard-table.csv is workable, but ACME will need to provision dedicated next-hop prefixes and ensure their on-prem routers accept the more-specifics. We'll need an ops runbook step to validate RIB acceptance and blackhole rules for the test shards.

2) Traffic mirroring overhead: many customer switches rate-limit mirror sessions. If ACME cannot mirror the full volume we should fall back to sampling (p: 1/10) and an expanded sequence-length-based sampling to capture long-context traffic. Put that option into the playbook as fallback.

3) KV cache isolation: tenant-prefixed keys are necessary but not sufficient. I want us to enforce a namespace prefix at the runtime kernel level (i.e., cache key builder) so even if an app bug tries to write the raw key it gets normalized. Also recommend shadow suffix pattern: "__shadow.<iso_ts>" to keep it observable in metrics.

4) Control-plane egress: ensure we only allow the minimal TLS endpoints (model-store, metrics, keystore) across the control-plane zone and pin to customer-allowed egress IPs. Document KMS/HSM IP ranges in the playbook.

I've added inline comments to the playbook draft and flagged a few Firewall rule templates that ACME will need.

—Irene
Senior Network Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: cloud-ops@acme.com
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational zones & shadow deploy patterns for private VPC runtime

Nice framing — two business items to capture before we run: 

- SLA/visibility: define expected latency impact on 95th pct for user requests during phased shadowing (10/50/100). We need this for the ACME SRE folks and our support runbooks.
- Rollback & safety: add an automated throttle that can cut mirrored traffic instantly and an immediate cache-clear play for shadow suffix namespaces. Also include a pre-flight list with acceptance criteria (RIB checks, mirror health, TTL policy verified).

If ACME agrees to these, green to proceed with Thursday 11am PT sync. Rachel, can you own the acceptance criteria doc?

—Marissa
Director, Customer Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: ACME Cloud Ops <cloud-ops@acme.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: eng@netsecure.io
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational zones & shadow deploy patterns for private VPC runtime

Rachel/Team —

Thanks for the design and the playbook — this looks promising. A few constraints from ACME infra: 
1) Mirror session limit: our top-of-rack chassis cap mirror sessions at ~10Gb/s per session; we'll need to sample for high-throughput pods.
2) BGP policy: we can accept the egress-shard table but require that each shard owner tag its next-hop with a community string for easy de-provisioning.
3) Maintenance window: for the full 100% shadow run we ask that this be scheduled in a low-traffic window (UTC 02:00–06:00) to reduce risk.

We'll join the Thursday sync. Marcus/Irene — ACME can provide a small set of router configs and mirror stats ahead of the call.

—Alex (on behalf of ACME Cloud Ops)
Cloud Operations Lead
Acme Corp
